name: platter
description: Catalog your vinyl records into your Discogs collection.

paragraphs: Scan a record's barcode and add it to your Discogs collection. Platter also tracks what your records are worth and how often you play them. It's a web app you can install to your phone's home screen, and it talks to Discogs directly from your browser.
No Discogs account? The demo has a sample collection to poke around in.
features: Scanning: barcode by camera or photo, or search by catalog number or artist and title. Batch mode queues scans (offline too) and adds them all at once.
Pressings: warns about duplicates and wantlist matches, and narrows down pressings by reading the runout or the spine.
Collection: grid or list, search, filters, sort, crates, and custom fields like condition, price, and location.
Value: Discogs prices per record, value over time, paid vs. now, and charts you can rearrange.
Listening: log plays, see what you play most and what you haven't touched in a year, and optionally scrobble to ListenBrainz.

whatItDoes.text: Scan a record's barcode and add it to your Discogs collection. Platter also tracks what your records are worth and how often you play them. It's a web app you can install to your phone's home screen, and it talks to Discogs directly from your browser.

requirements.text: Platter stores its data in the browser and calls api.discogs.com directly. "Log in with Discogs" uses OAuth, and a small Cloudflare Worker (worker/) signs requests with the app secret without ever seeing your data.
Locally, sign in with a personal access token or open /?demo.
